Quick response while I loop in Legal and Infra:\\\\n\\\\n- Short answer on residency: Redwood supports region pinning; production requests for an EU tenant are served from EU-hosted control plane & compute.\\\\n- Transient replication: there are a few edge behaviours (we\\u2019ll spell these out) but by default we do not replicate user request payloads to another region for normal serving.\\\\n\\\\nLooping in Marissa (Legal) for the DPA/addendum and Hannah (Infra) for the KV/cache details and exact operational guarantees. I\\u2019ll coordinate a short 30-min call if you prefer.\\\\n\\\\nNext steps: Marissa will share the subprocessor roster + a draft addendum; Hannah will describe caching/replication windows. I\\u2019ll schedule a call for tomorrow unless you prefer a different time.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014 Rohan\\\\nRohan Mehta\\\\nSenior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Kate Miller <kate.miller@optithera.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>\\\\nCc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com\\\\nDate: 2026-12-18T14:05:00-08:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Data residency confirmation + transient replication question\\\\n\\\\nKate, Rohan \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nThanks for flagging. Attaching the current subprocessor roster and a draft region-pinning addendum that we commonly use for EU-regulated customers. Key points for OptiThera:\\\\n\\\\n- DPA commitment: our standard DPA includes a region pinning clause that requires requests to be served from the customer-specified region. We are prepared to execute an addendum that makes this explicit for EU tenants.\\\\n\\\\n- Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists subprocessors and the region(s) where they operate. We can accept narrow scoping to EU-only subprocessors where feasible; some cloud providers have cross-region control plane components \\u2014 we've flagged those in the roster.\\\\n\\\\n- KMS & keys: customer keys (if using Redwood Dedicated or Private) remain in-region under the customer's KMS. For Hosted customers we offer per-region KMS-backed encryption; keys are created in-region and are not exported.\\\\n\\\\n- Logs & telemetry: application request logs and audit events can be configured to remain in-region for retention. By default we retain logs in-region for the pinned region and only replicate to other regions for customer-requested analytics exports or in the event of an approved DR failover.\\\\n\\\\n- Transient buffers / caches: see Hannah's note (below) for the infra specifics. Our legal posture is that transient in-memory caches are not considered persistent storage and are covered by the region-pinning addendum (we can add language that forbids cross-border in-memory copying except for documented failover scenarios).\\\\n\\\\nAttachments: subprocessor_roster_20261210.csv, region_pinning_addendum_draft.docx\\\\n\\\\nIf OptiThera wants hard contractual language around subprocessors and transient caches we can add a short clause in the addendum that requires Redwood to obtain written consent before any cross-border processing outside of the agreed failover plan. Let us know if you want a redline-ready version returned.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014 Marissa Cole\\\\nDirector, Legal \\u2014 Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Kate Miller <kate.miller@optithera.com>\\\\nTo: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>\\\\nCc: security@optithera.com\\\\nDate: 2026-12-19T09:15:00-08:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Data residency confirmation + transient replication question\\\\n\\\\nMarissa \\u2014 thanks for the quick turnaround and for the roster. A few clarifying questions from our compliance team (short bullets):\\\\n\\\\n- The regulator wants explicit confirmation that logs (including request/response metadata and application-level traces) will not leave the EU under normal operation. Can Redwood sign an addendum that states logs and telemetry are in-region and will only be exported with prior written approval?\\\\n\\\\n- Our ML team clarified: by \\\"KV cache\\\" they mean the model KV cache used during autoregressive generation (per-token hidden state). Under what circumstances could that be transferred cross-region? Is there any background process that moves warm caches between regions for efficiency?\\\\n\\\\n- If Redwood requires a transient cross-region step in an emergency (DR/failover), what is the escalation path and how long can data be present outside the pinned region? We need an SLA for notice + maximum transient window.\\\\n\\\\nAlso good to get confirmation of SOC 2 or audit evidence. Can you share the most recent SOC2 summary?\\\\n\\\\nAppreciate it \\u2014 Kate\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Kate Miller <kate.miller@optithera.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-12-19T14:30:00-08:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Data residency confirmation + transient replication question\\\\n\\\\nKate \\u2014 quick infra / operational answers from the serving/runtime side. Short bullets to address the ML team's specifics:\\\\n\\\\n- KV/prefix cache behaviour:\\\\n  * The model KV cache (per-request token state) is kept in-memory on the serving GPU process and is short-lived (typical lifetime: duration of the request + up to 60s for reuse by near-synchronous follow-up requests).\\\\n  * We do not proactively ship KV caches between regions for warm-up. There is no background \\u201cmove cache from EU cluster to US cluster\\u201d behaviour in normal operation.\\\\n  * Cache rehydration for serving is accomplished via in-region warm pools; warm-up (model weights, JIT caches) is done per-region.\\\\n\\\\n- Transient replication cases:\\\\n  * Cross-region replication of request payloads or caches occurs only during an orchestrated failover when the primary region is unavailable and the customer has agreed to failover options.\\\\n  * In those cases we trigger the failover plan, notify the customer via the configured escalation contacts, and the transient presence of data outside the pinned region is limited to the maintenance window required for recovery. We typically target < 4 hours for automated failover windows and < 24 hours for manual DR, but we can contractually cap this and add a notification SLA.\\\\n\\\\n- Logs & telemetry:\\\\n  * Audit logs for EU tenants are persisted to EU storage by default. We do not ship live audit logs to non-EU regions unless the customer has requested an export or the DPA addendum allows cross-region aggregation.\\\\n  * Operational metrics (anonymized cluster telemetry) are aggregated globally for reliability engineering; request-level logs remain in-region.\\\\n\\\\n- Options for stronger guarantee:\\\\n  * Redwood Dedicated: fully isolated EU GPU pools; no cross-region control-plane operations.\\\\n  * Redwood Private (VPC): can be deployed inside OptiThera's network with full control over egress.\\\\n\\\\nIf you want, we can add a clause in the addendum that: (1) forbids any cross-border copying of request/response logs or KV cache except under a written, pre-authorized failover procedure, and (2) defines a maximum transient window and notification SLA.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014 Hannah\\\\nSenior Systems Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Kate Miller <kate.miller@optithera.com>\\\\nCc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com\\\\nDate: 2026-12-20T17:45:00-08:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Data residency confirmation + transient replication question\\\\n\\\\nKate \\u2014 appreciate the quick follow-ups and all the great questions. Summary & proposed next steps so compliance has a single reference:\\\\n\\\\nSummary of commitments we can put into a DPA addendum:\\\\n- Residency: OptiThera EU tenant data (requests, generated content, request-level logs) will be processed and stored in EU-only infrastructure by default.\\\\n- Logs & telemetry: request/response logs and audit events will be written to EU storage; any export requires prior written consent.\\\\n- KV / prefix caches: in-memory only, never persisted outside the serving process. No cross-region cache warm-up in normal operation. Cross-region activity can only happen under an agreed failover plan.\\\\n- Failover: cross-region failover limited to customer-authorized scenarios; Redwood will provide notice to named contacts and will comply with a contractual cap on transient window (we recommend <= 4 hours for automated failover; we can accept a contractual cap).\\\\n- Subprocessors & keys: roster provided; per-region KMS options available.\\\\n\\\\nNext steps:\\\\n1) Marissa will send a redline-friendly addendum (attached draft). Short bullets to address the ML team's specifics:\\n\\n- KV/prefix cache behaviour:\\n  * The model KV cache (per-request token state) is kept in-memory on the serving GPU process and is short-lived (typical lifetime: duration of the request + up to 60s for reuse by near-synchronous follow-up requests).\\n  * We do not proactively ship KV caches between regions for warm-up.     "id": "dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)\",\n  \"space\": \"security-and-compliance\",\n  \"author\": \"Miles Thornton\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-12\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Victor Alvarez\",\n    \"Simran Kaur\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security\",\n    \"reliability\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"data-residency\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"audit-logging\",\n    \"enterprise\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:\\n- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.\\n- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.\\n- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).\\n\\nThis guidance is mandatory for:\\n- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.\\n- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).\\n- On-call execution and controlled failover tests (\\\"game days\\\").\\n\\n## Scope / Non-scope\\n**In scope**\\n- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.\\n- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.\\n- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.\\n\\n**Out of scope**\\n- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.\\n- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).\\n- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant\\u2019s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.\\n- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.\\n- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.\\n- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.\\n- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).\\n\\n## Security principles (must-haves)\\n1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.\\n2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.\\n3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.\\n4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct \\u201cwho/what/why/when/impact.\\u201d\\n5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).\\n\\n## Data residency policy\\n### Residency categories\\nRedwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):\\n\\n| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |\\n| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |\\n| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |\\n| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |\\n| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |\\n\\nNotes:\\n- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.\\n- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.\\n\\n### Default behavior by tier\\n- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.\\n- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.\\n- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer\\u2019s approved Dedicated regions.\\n- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer\\u2019s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.\\n\\n## Cross-region failover rules\\n### Hard rules (never violate)\\n1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant\\u2019s residency boundary.**\\n2) **Do not \\u201ctemporarily\\u201d violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.\\n3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:\\n   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND\\n   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND\\n   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.\\n\\n### Allowed failover patterns\\n- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):\\n  - EU-only: eu-west \\u2192 eu-central\\n  - US-only: us-east \\u2192 us-west\\n  - Custom: primary \\u2192 secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)\\n- **Region-pinned tenants**:\\n  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.\\n\\n### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)\\nRouting may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:\\n- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating \\u201cbest\\u201d region.\\n- If the \\u201cbest available\\u201d region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not \\u201cfail over.\\u201d\\n\\n## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)\\n### Residency gating in the policy engine\\nThe policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):\\n- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.\\n- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions \\u2229 allowed_regions`.\\n- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:\\n  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or\\n  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.\\n\\nSecurity requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no \\u201cemergency override\\u201d without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).\\n\\n### Configuration source of truth\\nFor Hosted and Dedicated:\\n- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:\\n  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).\\n  - Immutable change history.\\n  - Rollback support.\\n\\n### Dedicated-specific constraints\\nDedicated customers may have:\\n- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.\\n- Explicit \\u201cno failover without approval\\u201d requirements.\\n\\nFailover automation for Dedicated must:\\n- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).\\n- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.\\n\\n## Audit logging requirements\\n### What must be logged\\nAll systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:\\n- Recommendation (dry-run computation)\\n- Execution (policy flip applied)\\n- Rollback (automated or manual)\\n- Override (operator forcing a decision)\\n- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)\\n\\n### Required fields (minimum)\\nEach audit event must include (as applicable):\\n- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked\\n- **timestamp_utc**\\n- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)\\n- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated\\n- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom\\n- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)\\n- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put\\n- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual\\n- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs\\n- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>\\n- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied\\n- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision\\n- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID\\n\\n### Retention and access\\n- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.\\n- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **\\u2265 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.\\n- Access must be restricted to:\\n  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need\\n  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations\\n  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)\\n\\n### Data minimization\\nAudit events must not include:\\n- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.\\n- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).\\n\\nIf request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.\\n\\n## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers\\n### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary\\nExample: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.\\n- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.\\n- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.\\n  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)\\n  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness\\n  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy\\n\\n### Communication expectations (Enterprise)\\n- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.\\n- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.\\n- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:\\n  - Pull audit events for the tenant\\n  - Validate residency gating decisions\\n  - Engage Security and Support escalation\\n\\n## Controlled failover tests (\\u201cgame days\\u201d) security requirements\\nPrior to production tests:\\n1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.\\n2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.\\n3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.\\n4) Validate that \\u201cblocked due to residency\\u201d is observable (metric + audit event).\\n\\nDuring the test:\\n- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.\\n\\nAfter the test:\\n- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.\\n\\n## Operational checklist (on-call)\\nWhen failover automation suggests a policy change:\\n1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.\\n2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.\\n3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).\\n4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).\\n5) Execute or approve.\\n6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.\\n\\n## Examples\\n### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident\\n- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)\\n- Required action:\\n  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)\\n  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration\\n  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry\\n\\n### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: any region\\n- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.\\n\\n### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: eu-west only\\n- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.\\n\\n## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)\\nMinimum dashboards/alerts needed:\\n- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier\\n- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)\\n- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)\\n- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)\\n\\n## Ownership and change control\\n- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)\\n- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)\\n- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)\\n\\nChanges to this document require review from:\\n- Security & Compliance\\n- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)\\n- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)\\n\\n## Open questions / follow-ups\\n- Define a standard \\u201ccustom boundary\\u201d representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.\\n- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.\\n- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: security-and-compliance\n\n* * private * * : residency enforcement is the customer ’ s responsibility, but redwood - provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document. # # cross - region failover rules # # # hard rules ( never violate ) 1 ) * * do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant ’ s residency boundary. * * 2 ) * * do not “ temporarily ” violate residency to restore availability. * * if no in - boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary. 3 ) * * do not change residency boundaries during an incident * * to work around a capacity / regional outage unless : - approved by security ( delegate on - call ) and - approved by the customer ( if enterprise / regulated ) and - documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.",

document.title: Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)

{
  "title": "Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Miles Thornton",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "created_at": "2026-01-07",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-12",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Victor Alvarez",
    "Simran Kaur"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "security",
    "reliability",
    "failover",
    "data-residency",
    "routing",
    "audit-logging",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:
- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.
- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.
- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).

This guidance is mandatory for:
- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.
- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).
- On-call execution and controlled failover tests ("game days").

## Scope / Non-scope
**In scope**
- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.
- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.
- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.

**Out of scope**
- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.
- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).

## Definitions
- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).
- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant’s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.
- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.
- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.
- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.
- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).

## Security principles (must-haves)
1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.
2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.
3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.
4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct “who/what/why/when/impact.”
5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).

## Data residency policy
### Residency categories
Redwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):

| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |
| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |
| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |
| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |
| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |

Notes:
- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.
- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.

### Default behavior by tier
- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.
- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.
- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer’s approved Dedicated regions.
- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer’s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.

## Cross-region failover rules
### Hard rules (never violate)
1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant’s residency boundary.**
2) **Do not “temporarily” violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.
3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:
   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND
   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND
   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.

### Allowed failover patterns
- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):
  - EU-only: eu-west → eu-central
  - US-only: us-east → us-west
  - Custom: primary → secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)
- **Region-pinned tenants**:
  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.

### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)
Routing may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:
- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating “best” region.
- If the “best available” region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not “fail over.”

## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)
### Residency gating in the policy engine
The policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):
- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.
- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions ∩ allowed_regions`.
- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:
  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or
  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.

Security requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no “emergency override” without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).

### Configuration source of truth
For Hosted and Dedicated:
- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:
  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).
  - Immutable change history.
  - Rollback support.

### Dedicated-specific constraints
Dedicated customers may have:
- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.
- Explicit “no failover without approval” requirements.

Failover automation for Dedicated must:
- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).
- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.

## Audit logging requirements
### What must be logged
All systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:
- Recommendation (dry-run computation)
- Execution (policy flip applied)
- Rollback (automated or manual)
- Override (operator forcing a decision)
- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)

### Required fields (minimum)
Each audit event must include (as applicable):
- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked
- **timestamp_utc**
- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)
- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated
- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom
- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)
- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put
- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual
- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs
- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>
- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied
- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision
- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID

### Retention and access
- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.
- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **≥ 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.
- Access must be restricted to:
  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need
  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations
  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)

### Data minimization
Audit events must not include:
- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.
- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).

If request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.

## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers
### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary
Example: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.
- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.
- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.
  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)
  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness
  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy

### Communication expectations (Enterprise)
- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.
- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.
- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:
  - Pull audit events for the tenant
  - Validate residency gating decisions
  - Engage Security and Support escalation

## Controlled failover tests (“game days”) security requirements
Prior to production tests:
1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.
2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.
3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.
4) Validate that “blocked due to residency” is observable (metric + audit event).

During the test:
- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.

After the test:
- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.

## Operational checklist (on-call)
When failover automation suggests a policy change:
1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.
2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.
3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).
4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).
5) Execute or approve.
6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.

## Examples
### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident
- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)
- Required action:
  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)
  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration
  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry

### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: any region
- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.

### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: eu-west only
- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.

## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)
Minimum dashboards/alerts needed:
- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier
- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)
- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)
- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)

## Ownership and change control
- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)
- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)
- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)

Changes to this document require review from:
- Security & Compliance
- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)
- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Define a standard “custom boundary” representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.
- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.
- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).

    "title": "Introduce data-residency-guards, KMS key scoping, and RBAC v2 role mapping",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"86107\",\n  \"title\": \"Introduce data-residency-guards, KMS key scoping, and RBAC v2 role mapping\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-14\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-02\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-03-02\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/security/data-residency-kms-rbac-v2\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Luca Rivera\",\n    \"Priya Nair\",\n    \"Owen Park\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"rbac\",\n    \"kms\",\n    \"audit\",\n    \"privacy\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4821\",\n    \"SEC-134\",\n    \"PM-210\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-7890\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"18\",\n  \"additions\": \"1128\",\n  \"deletions\": \"312\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Tenant-scoped KMS enforcement and data-residency guards; RBAC v2 mapping now honors region tags; audit header validation for routed requests; migration tool for existing customer KMS bindings.\",\n  \"description\": \"Summary: This PR implements tenant-aware data residency controls (aka 'residency-guards'), scopes KMS key usage to tenant+region, and extends RBAC v2 role mappings to carry region annotations. Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested hard guarantees that keys and audit streams remain in-customer regions and that role grants cannot be used to bypass residency rules. This change closes gaps discovered during compliance reviews and a recent support investigation (SUP-7890). High level changes: 1) Residency guard middleware: routes requests by tenant geo-tag and enforces region pinning policies; rejects or routes to fallback when policy mismatch. 2) KMS scoping: KMS key references now require a tenant and region qualifier; server-side validation added to key lookup path and crypto plugins updated to reject cross-region key usage. 3) RBAC v2 mapping: role mappings accept an optional region_claim attribute which restricts tokens to the specified region; evaluation engine updated to intersect tenant region and role region. 4) Audit propagation: introduced X-Redwood-Audit-Region header enforcement and enriched audit log entries with region and key_id. 5) Migration tooling: included kms-region-migrate script that converts legacy key bindings and emits a report for customer review. 6) Tests & CI: new unit and integration tests including simulated multi-region tenants and negative tests for mis-scoped keys. Commits (high level): - 2a1f7bd: residency guard middleware and policy model - 7b4e2c1: KMS validation and plugin API changes - 9c2d5f8: RBAC v2 evaluator region handling and mapping docs - d45a8e3: audit header enforcement and log enrichment - f1b9c02: kms-region-migrate tool and migration tests - 0e3a91d: add e2e scenarios to private installer suite Changed areas/files (high level): - src/security/residency/guard.go: new middleware and policy loader - proto/policy/residency.proto: policy schema additions - internal/kms/provider.go: key scoping and validation logic (illustrative snippet: if key.Region != request.Region { return ErrRegionMismatch }) - services/authn/rbac/v2/mapping.go: region_claim checks and eval updates - cmd/kms-region-migrate/main.go: migration entrypoint and report exporter - infra/priv-installer/e2e/residency_test.go: e2e scenarios for on-prem installer - docs/security/data-residency.md: design and operator runbook Review notes and conversation: - Priya: \\\"Can we ensure the middleware short-circuits before any key material is fetched?\\\" Author reply: \\\"Yes, guard checks run in the request admission path; added unit test and comment to make ordering explicit.\\\" - Luca: \\\"Migration tool looks good, but add a dry-run mode and a CSV report.\\\" Author reply: \\\"Added --dry-run and CSV output; report includes before/after key bindings.\\\" - Owen: \\\"What happens if a region label is missing on older tenants?\\\" Author reply: \\\"Policy default is inbound: tenants without explicit region remain in 'unscoped' bucket and are blocked from KMS operations until migration; we added an operator-facing migration guide.\\\" - Priya requested a security review for crypto plugin changes, later approved after one minor naming nit. CI: initial runs failed on lint due to naming of a test variable; fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e). Performance: small runtime overhead for residency checks (~0.6ms median per request in microbench), measured in tests and within SLO for targeted customers. Backwards compatibility: the KMS provider API introduces a non-breaking optional parameter for region; we included shims in legacy adapters. Migration: kms-region-migrate included and tested; migration has to be scheduled by operator and can be rolled back by restoring previous binding snapshot. Security considerations: added threat mitigation section to docs and required an ACL check prior to migration script execution. Merge details: PR approved by reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-02. Squash commit message: \\\"security: add data-residency guards, KMS scoping, RBAC v2 region mapping\\\" Follow-ups: - ENG-4821: rollout plan for Dedicated clusters and Private installer upgrades - SEC-134: audit rule to alert on any requests rejected by residency guard - PM-210: UI controls to show tenant region and migration status in console Known limitations: cross-region read-only audit streams are not migrated automatically; operator action required. Notes for release: this change should be rolled out to staging + canary before full prod; include operators on migration schedule. Related: references SUP-7890 and internal design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/RESIDENCY-DESIGN (internal).\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11\"\n}",

{
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "86107",
  "title": "Introduce data-residency-guards, KMS key scoping, and RBAC v2 role mapping",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "created_at": "2026-02-14",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-02",
  "merged_at": "2026-03-02",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/security/data-residency-kms-rbac-v2",
  "reviewers": [
    "Luca Rivera",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Owen Park"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "security",
    "compliance",
    "rbac",
    "kms",
    "audit",
    "privacy"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4821",
    "SEC-134",
    "PM-210"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-7890"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "18",
  "additions": "1128",
  "deletions": "312",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "release_notes": "Tenant-scoped KMS enforcement and data-residency guards; RBAC v2 mapping now honors region tags; audit header validation for routed requests; migration tool for existing customer KMS bindings.",
  "description": "Summary: This PR implements tenant-aware data residency controls (aka 'residency-guards'), scopes KMS key usage to tenant+region, and extends RBAC v2 role mappings to carry region annotations. Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested hard guarantees that keys and audit streams remain in-customer regions and that role grants cannot be used to bypass residency rules. This change closes gaps discovered during compliance reviews and a recent support investigation (SUP-7890). High level changes: 1) Residency guard middleware: routes requests by tenant geo-tag and enforces region pinning policies; rejects or routes to fallback when policy mismatch. 2) KMS scoping: KMS key references now require a tenant and region qualifier; server-side validation added to key lookup path and crypto plugins updated to reject cross-region key usage. 3) RBAC v2 mapping: role mappings accept an optional region_claim attribute which restricts tokens to the specified region; evaluation engine updated to intersect tenant region and role region. 4) Audit propagation: introduced X-Redwood-Audit-Region header enforcement and enriched audit log entries with region and key_id. 5) Migration tooling: included kms-region-migrate script that converts legacy key bindings and emits a report for customer review. 6) Tests & CI: new unit and integration tests including simulated multi-region tenants and negative tests for mis-scoped keys. Commits (high level): - 2a1f7bd: residency guard middleware and policy model - 7b4e2c1: KMS validation and plugin API changes - 9c2d5f8: RBAC v2 evaluator region handling and mapping docs - d45a8e3: audit header enforcement and log enrichment - f1b9c02: kms-region-migrate tool and migration tests - 0e3a91d: add e2e scenarios to private installer suite Changed areas/files (high level): - src/security/residency/guard.go: new middleware and policy loader - proto/policy/residency.proto: policy schema additions - internal/kms/provider.go: key scoping and validation logic (illustrative snippet: if key.Region != request.Region { return ErrRegionMismatch }) - services/authn/rbac/v2/mapping.go: region_claim checks and eval updates - cmd/kms-region-migrate/main.go: migration entrypoint and report exporter - infra/priv-installer/e2e/residency_test.go: e2e scenarios for on-prem installer - docs/security/data-residency.md: design and operator runbook Review notes and conversation: - Priya: \"Can we ensure the middleware short-circuits before any key material is fetched?\" Author reply: \"Yes, guard checks run in the request admission path; added unit test and comment to make ordering explicit.\" - Luca: \"Migration tool looks good, but add a dry-run mode and a CSV report.\" Author reply: \"Added --dry-run and CSV output; report includes before/after key bindings.\" - Owen: \"What happens if a region label is missing on older tenants?\" Author reply: \"Policy default is inbound: tenants without explicit region remain in 'unscoped' bucket and are blocked from KMS operations until migration; we added an operator-facing migration guide.\" - Priya requested a security review for crypto plugin changes, later approved after one minor naming nit. CI: initial runs failed on lint due to naming of a test variable; fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e). Performance: small runtime overhead for residency checks (~0.6ms median per request in microbench), measured in tests and within SLO for targeted customers. Backwards compatibility: the KMS provider API introduces a non-breaking optional parameter for region; we included shims in legacy adapters. Migration: kms-region-migrate included and tested; migration has to be scheduled by operator and can be rolled back by restoring previous binding snapshot. Security considerations: added threat mitigation section to docs and required an ACL check prior to migration script execution. Merge details: PR approved by reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-02. Squash commit message: \"security: add data-residency guards, KMS scoping, RBAC v2 region mapping\" Follow-ups: - ENG-4821: rollout plan for Dedicated clusters and Private installer upgrades - SEC-134: audit rule to alert on any requests rejected by residency guard - PM-210: UI controls to show tenant region and migration status in console Known limitations: cross-region read-only audit streams are not migrated automatically; operator action required. Notes for release: this change should be rolled out to staging + canary before full prod; include operators on migration schedule. Related: references SUP-7890 and internal design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/RESIDENCY-DESIGN (internal).",

  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "release_notes"
  ],

# EU residency failover — interview notes (temporary)

Status: provisional working state. Do not index or publish.

## Provisional questions

- Does the customer's executed Hosted agreement encode EU-only, single-region pinning, a custom boundary, or global routing? Do not infer from “EU customer.”
- Which regions are currently in the tenant's authoritative `allowed_regions`, and is any approval hook required?
- Is the KMS binding Redwood-managed or customer-managed, and do its tenant and region qualifiers match every allowed failover target?
- Can Support retrieve recommend/execute/rollback/blocked audit events for the incident window, including change ID, actor, approval state, evidence references, target, decision, and key identifier?
- Are content-bearing logs restricted to the residency boundary while content-free operational metrics are centrally aggregated?
- Is the customer asking about data-plane processing, control-plane metadata, backups, audit exports, or all four?
- Which contractual addendum and customer-approved failover procedure are executed and current?

## Discarded interpretations

- Discarded: “Enterprise Hosted is EU-only by default.” The security boundary standard says Hosted defaults to Global unless an enforceable contractual residency policy is configured.
- Discarded: “EU-only means eu-west only.” EU-only may allow multiple explicitly configured EU regions; single-region behavior is a separate region-pinned mode.
- Discarded: “Disaster recovery automatically permits US processing.” Out-of-boundary routing requires an approved boundary change and customer approval; otherwise the system must degrade or stay put.
- Discarded: “A healthy destination is sufficient.” The target must also be allow-listed, capacity-ready, compatible, KMS-valid, and auditable.
- Discarded: “KMS follows traffic automatically.” Implemented controls bind keys to tenant and region and reject cross-region key use; legacy/migration state must be checked.
- Discarded: “Audit retention is safe to quote generically.” Retention varies by policy/package/contract and remains an explicit uncertainty; Support must not promise a duration without the executed agreement.
- Discarded: “A proposed email addendum is a universal contract.” Customer-specific email language is supporting legal posture, not proof of another customer's executed terms.

## Follow-ups

- Ask Legal/Account team to identify the executed residency clause and any written pre-authorized failover procedure.
- Ask Routing On-Call to confirm live policy revision, allowed regions, approval hooks, and drift status.
- Ask Security/KMS owner to confirm binding migration status and region-qualified key availability at each target.
- Ask Observability to confirm audit delivery health and any gaps in cross-region read-only audit stream migration.
- Resolve the published security document's open question about enterprise audit-retention defaults before giving any retention duration.
- Confirm whether Support has a redacted export procedure for customer-facing evidence.

# EU residency failover response for Customer Support

Owner: Platform Engineering  
Audience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  
Scope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment

## Reviewed support rule

Do not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.

## Supported routing modes

- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.
- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.
- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.
- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.
- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).

## Consent and deny defaults

Routing evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.

For an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).

## KMS behavior

The enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Audit behavior

Every failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.

Capture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.

Do not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Support validation steps

1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.
2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.
3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.
4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.
5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.
6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.
7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.
8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.

Sources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).

## Escalate when

- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.
- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.
- A boundary change is requested during an incident.
- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.
- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.
- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.
- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.
- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.

Engage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.

## Customer-response template

“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.
- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.
- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.
- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.
- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.

Additional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).

RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Audit behavior

Every failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.

Capture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.

Do not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Support validation steps

1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.
2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.
3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.
4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.
5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.
6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.
7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.
8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.

Sources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).

## Escalate when

- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.
- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.
- A boundary change is requested during an incident.
- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.
- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.
- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.
- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.
- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.

Engage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.

## Customer-response template

“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.
- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.
- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.
- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.
- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.

Additional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).

arguments.summary: For Hosted API residency questions, Support must verify the executed customer agreement and live enforceable allowed-region policy before making a claim. EU-only, region-pinned, and custom-boundary traffic may fail over only to healthy, capable, explicitly allowed targets with valid tenant+region KMS bindings and complete audit evidence. If no allowed target is usable, deny out-of-boundary routing and degrade or stay put; never describe disaster recovery as an automatic consent waiver. Boundary expansion requires Security and applicable customer approval plus an auditable time-scoped change. Do not promise retention, backup, notification, or transient-window terms without the executed agreement.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Reviewed Customer Support rule for Hosted EU residency failover\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/reviewed-customer-support-rule-for-hosted-eu-residency-failover-22c36d34.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Jada Williams\n\n# Reviewed Customer Support rule for Hosted EU residency failover\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-04T05:06:24.876507+00:00\nConfidence: 0.96\nOwner: Jada Williams\nTags: customer-support, hosted-api, eu-residency, failover, kms, audit\n\n## Summary\n\nFor Hosted API residency questions, Support must verify the executed customer agreement and live enforceable allowed-region policy before making a claim. EU-only, region-pinned, and custom-boundary traffic may fail over only to healthy, capable, explicitly allowed targets with valid tenant+region KMS bindings and complete audit evidence. If no allowed target is usable, deny out-of-boundary routing and degrade or stay put; never describe disaster recovery as an automatic consent waiver. Boundary expansion requires Security and applicable customer approval plus an auditable time-scoped change. Do not promise retention, backup, notification, or transient-window terms without the executed agreement.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\n- workspace_a8999f9c18bb9db043105036\n- /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json\n- dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\n- /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json\n- dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc\n- /knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json\n- dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11\n- /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json\n- dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n# EU residency failover response for Customer Support\n\nOwner: Platform Engineering  \nAudience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  \nScope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment\n\n## Reviewed support rule\n\nDo not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.\n- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.\n- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.\n- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.\n- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.",
