              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\nwhile communicating the impairment.\n- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.\n- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).\n\n## Consent and deny defaults\n\nRouting evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.\n\nFor an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\ndescribe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.\n\nFor an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).\n\n## KMS behavior\n\nThe enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.\n\nSupport must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.\n\nSource: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).",

              "ordinal": 3,
              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n[Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).\n\n## Audit behavior\n\nEvery failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.\n\nCapture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.\n\nDo not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\nMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).\n\n## Support validation steps\n\n1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.\n2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.\n3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.\n4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.\n5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.\n6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.\n7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.\n8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.\n\nSources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).\n\n## Escalate when",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n25ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).\n\n## Escalate when\n\n- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.\n- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.\n- A boundary change is requested during an incident.\n- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.\n- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.\n- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.\n- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.\n- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.\n\nEngage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.\n\n## Customer-response template\n\n“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”\n\n## Uncertainty and limits",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”\n\n## Uncertainty and limits\n\n- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.\n- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.\n- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.\n- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.\n- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.\n\nAdditional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).",

            "content": "# EU residency failover — interview notes (temporary)\n\nStatus: provisional working state. Do not index or publish.\n\n## Provisional questions\n\n- Does the customer's executed Hosted agreement encode EU-only, single-region pinning, a custom boundary, or global routing? Do not infer from “EU customer.”\n- Which regions are currently in the tenant's authoritative `allowed_regions`, and is any approval hook required?\n- Is the KMS binding Redwood-managed or customer-managed, and do its tenant and region qualifiers match every allowed failover target?\n- Can Support retrieve recommend/execute/rollback/blocked audit events for the incident window, including change ID, actor, approval state, evidence references, target, decision, and key identifier?\n- Are content-bearing logs restricted to the residency boundary while content-free operational metrics are centrally aggregated?\n- Is the customer asking about data-plane processing, control-plane metadata, backups, audit exports, or all four?\n- Which contractual addendum and customer-approved failover procedure are executed and current?\n\n## Discarded interpretations\n\n- Discarded: “Enterprise Hosted is EU-only by default.” The security boundary standard says Hosted defaults to Global unless an enforceable contractual residency policy is configured.\n- Discarded: “EU-only means eu-west only.” EU-only may allow multiple explicitly configured EU regions; single-region behavior is a separate region-pinned mode.\n- Discarded: “Disaster recovery automatically permits US processing.” Out-of-boundary routing requires an approved boundary change and customer approval; otherwise the system must degrade or stay put.\n- Discarded: “A healthy destination is sufficient.” The target must also be allow-listed, capacity-ready, compatible, KMS-valid, and auditable.\n- Discarded: “KMS follows traffic automatically.” Implemented controls bind keys to tenant and region and reject cross-region key use; legacy/migration state must be checked.\n- Discarded: “Audit retention is safe to quote generically.” Retention varies by policy/package/contract and remains an explicit uncertainty; Support must not promise a duration without the executed agreement.\n- Discarded: “A proposed email addendum is a universal contract.” Customer-specific email language is supporting legal posture, not proof of another customer's executed terms.\n\n## Follow-ups\n\n- Ask Legal/Account team to identify the executed residency clause and any written pre-authorized failover procedure.\n- Ask Routing On-Call to confirm live policy revision, allowed regions, approval hooks, and drift status.\n- Ask Security/KMS owner to confirm binding migration status and region-qualified key availability at each target.\n- Ask Observability to confirm audit delivery health and any gaps in cross-region read-only audit stream migration.\n- Resolve the published security document's open question about enterprise audit-retention defaults before giving any retention duration.\n- Confirm whether Support has a redacted export procedure for customer-facing evidence.\n\n## Evidence consulted\n\n- `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json` (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`)\n- `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json` (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`)\n- `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json` (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`)\n- `/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json` (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`)\n- `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json` (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`)\n",

            "content": "# EU residency failover response for Customer Support\n\nOwner: Platform Engineering  \nAudience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  \nScope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment\n\n## Reviewed support rule\n\nDo not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.\n- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.\n- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.\n- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.\n- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).\n\n## Consent and deny defaults\n\nRouting evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.\n\nFor an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).\n\n## KMS behavior\n\nThe enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore",

            "content": ", an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.\n\nSupport must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.\n\nSource: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).\n\n## Audit behavior\n\nEvery failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.\n\nCapture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.\n\nDo not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).\n\n## Support validation steps\n\n1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.\n2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.\n3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.\n4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.\n5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.\n6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.\n7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.\n8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.\n\nSources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/fail",

            "content": "over-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).\n\n## Escalate when\n\n- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.\n- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.\n- A boundary change is requested during an incident.\n- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.\n- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.\n- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.\n- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.\n- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.\n\nEngage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.\n\n## Customer-response template\n\n“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”\n\n## Uncertainty and limits\n\n- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.\n- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.\n- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.\n- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.\n- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.\n\nAdditional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).\n",

            "content": "# Reviewed Customer Support rule for Hosted EU residency failover\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-04T05:06:24.876507+00:00\nConfidence: 0.96\nOwner: Jada Williams\nTags: customer-support, hosted-api, eu-residency, failover, kms, audit\n\n## Summary\n\nFor Hosted API residency questions, Support must verify the executed customer agreement and live enforceable allowed-region policy before making a claim. EU-only, region-pinned, and custom-boundary traffic may fail over only to healthy, capable, explicitly allowed targets with valid tenant+region KMS bindings and complete audit evidence. If no allowed target is usable, deny out-of-boundary routing and degrade or stay put; never describe disaster recovery as an automatic consent waiver. Boundary expansion requires Security and applicable customer approval plus an auditable time-scoped change. Do not promise retention, backup, notification, or transient-window terms without the executed agreement.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\n- workspace_a8999f9c18bb9db043105036\n- /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json\n- dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\n- /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json\n- dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc\n- /knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json\n- dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11\n- /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json\n- dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4\n",

# EU residency failover response for Customer Support

Owner: Platform Engineering  
Audience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  
Scope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment

## Reviewed support rule

Do not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.

## Supported routing modes

- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.
- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.
- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.
- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.
- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.

## Consent and deny defaults

Routing evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.

For an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.

## KMS behavior

The enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Audit behavior

Every failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.

Capture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.

Do not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.

## Support validation steps

1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.
2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.
3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.
4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.
5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.
6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.
7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.
8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.

## Escalate when

## Escalate when

- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.
- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.
- A boundary change is requested during an incident.
- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.
- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.
- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.
- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.
- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.

Engage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.

## Customer-response template

“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.
- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.
- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.
- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.
- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.

# EU residency failover — interview notes (temporary)

Status: provisional working state. Do not index or publish.

## Provisional questions

- Does the customer's executed Hosted agreement encode EU-only, single-region pinning, a custom boundary, or global routing? Do not infer from “EU customer.”
- Which regions are currently in the tenant's authoritative `allowed_regions`, and is any approval hook required?
- Is the KMS binding Redwood-managed or customer-managed, and do its tenant and region qualifiers match every allowed failover target?
- Can Support retrieve recommend/execute/rollback/blocked audit events for the incident window, including change ID, actor, approval state, evidence references, target, decision, and key identifier?
- Are content-bearing logs restricted to the residency boundary while content-free operational metrics are centrally aggregated?
- Is the customer asking about data-plane processing, control-plane metadata, backups, audit exports, or all four?
- Which contractual addendum and customer-approved failover procedure are executed and current?

## Discarded interpretations

- Discarded: “Enterprise Hosted is EU-only by default.” The security boundary standard says Hosted defaults to Global unless an enforceable contractual residency policy is configured.
- Discarded: “EU-only means eu-west only.” EU-only may allow multiple explicitly configured EU regions; single-region behavior is a separate region-pinned mode.
- Discarded: “Disaster recovery automatically permits US processing.” Out-of-boundary routing requires an approved boundary change and customer approval; otherwise the system must degrade or stay put.
- Discarded: “A healthy destination is sufficient.” The target must also be allow-listed, capacity-ready, compatible, KMS-valid, and auditable.
- Discarded: “KMS follows traffic automatically.” Implemented controls bind keys to tenant and region and reject cross-region key use; legacy/migration state must be checked.
- Discarded: “Audit retention is safe to quote generically.” Retention varies by policy/package/contract and remains an explicit uncertainty; Support must not promise a duration without the executed agreement.
- Discarded: “A proposed email addendum is a universal contract.” Customer-specific email language is supporting legal posture, not proof of another customer's executed terms.

## Follow-ups

- Ask Legal/Account team to identify the executed residency clause and any written pre-authorized failover procedure.
- Ask Routing On-Call to confirm live policy revision, allowed regions, approval hooks, and drift status.
- Ask Security/KMS owner to confirm binding migration status and region-qualified key availability at each target.
- Ask Observability to confirm audit delivery health and any gaps in cross-region read-only audit stream migration.
- Resolve the published security document's open question about enterprise audit-retention defaults before giving any retention duration.
- Confirm whether Support has a redacted export procedure for customer-facing evidence.

# EU residency failover response for Customer Support

Owner: Platform Engineering  
Audience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  
Scope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment

## Reviewed support rule

Do not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.

## Supported routing modes

- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.
- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.
- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.
- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.
- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).

## Consent and deny defaults

Routing evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.

For an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).

## KMS behavior

The enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore

, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Audit behavior

Every failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.

Capture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.

Do not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Support validation steps

1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.
2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.
3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.
4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.
5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.
6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.
7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.
8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.

Sources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/fail

over-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).

## Escalate when

- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.
- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.
- A boundary change is requested during an incident.
- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.
- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.
- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.
- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.
- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.

Engage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.

## Customer-response template

“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.
- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.
- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.
- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.
- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.

Additional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\nwhile communicating the impairment.\n- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.\n- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).\n\n## Consent and deny defaults\n\nRouting evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.\n\nFor an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\ndescribe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.\n\nFor an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.\n\nSources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).\n\n## KMS behavior\n\nThe enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.\n\nSupport must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.\n\nSource: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).",

Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.\n8.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n25ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).\n\n## Escalate when\n\n- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.\n- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.\n- A boundary change is requested during an incident.\n- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.\n- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.\n- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.\n- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.\n- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.\n\nEngage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.\n\n## Customer-response template\n\n“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”\n\n## Uncertainty and limits",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”\n\n## Uncertainty and limits\n\n- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.\n- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.\n- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.\n- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.\n- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.\n\nAdditional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).",

document.title: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support
document.content:
# EU residency failover response for Customer Support

Owner: Platform Engineering  
Audience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  
Scope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment

## Reviewed support rule

Do not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.

## Supported routing modes

- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.
- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.
- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.
- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.
- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`).

## Consent and deny defaults

Routing evaluates healthy candidates against the tenant's explicit `allowed_regions`. Residency gating is an absolute precondition. Cross-region within the allowed boundary needs no new residency exception, although tenant-specific approval hooks may still apply. A target outside the current boundary must be denied unless the boundary change is approved by Security, approved by the customer where required, and recorded with timestamps and scope. Support must never describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.

For an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).

## KMS behavior

The enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Audit behavior

Every failover recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked attempt must produce a structured event. Validate at least: event type and UTC timestamp; tenant/org and tier; residency category; primary and target region; failover/degrade/stay-put decision; reason; evidence references; actor; approval state; routing change ID; and incident/correlation IDs. KMS-aware enforcement also enriches records with region and key ID.

Capture the controller change ID and supporting region-health, burn-rate, reachability, and capacity evidence in the incident timeline. If the expected audit event is missing, record actions and timestamps manually, file with the failover-controller team, and escalate rather than representing the action as fully evidenced.

Do not promise a generic retention period. The security standard contains package-dependent values and an unresolved follow-up about enterprise defaults; the customer-facing duration must come from the executed agreement or approved compliance package. Content-bearing logs/traces remain within an enforced boundary; content-free operational metrics may be aggregated centrally, subject to classification policy.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).

## Support validation steps

1. Identify the customer, tenant/org ID, Hosted route/model group, impacted region, and incident window.
2. Obtain the executed contract/addendum. Classify the commitment as Global, EU-only, region-pinned, or custom; do not infer it from geography or tier.
3. Ask Routing On-Call for the live policy revision, `allowed_regions`, approval hooks, and drift status. Confirm the proposed target is in the set.
4. Confirm the target is healthy, capacity-ready, model/feature compatible, and not concurrently degraded. Require the controller dry-run before execution.
5. Verify the KMS mode and that the tenant+region key binding is valid at the target before any shift.
6. Pull audit events for recommendation, execution or block/degrade, and any rollback. Match change ID, actor, approvals, target, decision, evidence, incident ID, region, and key ID.
7. Check customer-visible results: representative synthetic requests, error/streaming behavior, destination saturation, and policy-flip stability.
8. Respond with verified facts only: configured boundary, whether traffic stayed inside it, action/decision, evidence/change ID, current impact, and next update path. Use approved redacted exports for customer evidence.

Sources: [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`); [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`).

## Escalate when

- Contract language and live policy disagree, or the executed addendum cannot be located.
- An EU-only decision or audit trail shows a non-EU target, or the customer reports apparent cross-boundary processing.
- A boundary change is requested during an incident.
- The KMS tenant/region binding is missing, mismatched, legacy/unmigrated, or key access occurs before residency admission.
- Audit events, approval evidence, change IDs, or delivery health are missing.
- Routing drifts from the policy, a deterministic block does not occur, or a supposedly pinned request is served elsewhere.
- Destination capacity/compatibility is uncertain, dry-run recommends hold, signals conflict, or controller/control-plane health is impaired.
- Support is asked to promise retention, notification timing, transient windows, backups, or export behavior not stated in the executed agreement.

Engage Routing On-Call for policy semantics, Security for residency/approval or suspected boundary breach, KMS/Crypto owner for bindings, Control Plane On-Call for controller health, Observability for audit delivery, and Legal/Account for contract interpretation. Treat actual out-of-boundary data-plane processing during a controlled test as a security incident under the published boundary standard.

## Customer-response template

“Your Hosted API behavior is governed by the residency boundary in your executed agreement and the corresponding enforced routing policy. We are validating the live allowed-region set, KMS binding, and failover audit events for this incident. If your tenant is configured EU-only or region-pinned, Redwood will not silently route data-plane traffic outside that boundary; when no permitted target is available, the service degrades or remains in-region. We will confirm the observed routing decision and supporting change/audit identifiers after validation.”

## Uncertainty and limits

- The correct customer commitment is the executed agreement plus live enforceable policy, not a generic sales statement.
- “EU-only” does not by itself prove a particular region list; read the tenant configuration.
- The cited Gmail contract discussion supports the legal posture that non-EU failover paths require documented customer consent, but it is customer-specific correspondence and is not a universal executed agreement.
- KMS enforcement is implemented, but tenant migration/binding state and read-only audit-stream migration require live verification.
- Audit retention, backup replication, notification timing, and maximum transient failover windows are contract/package-specific. This runbook intentionally makes no new promise or date.

Additional legal-posture source: [Questions on data residency, retention, and cross-border transfers](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) (`dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4`).

  "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover Response for Customer Support\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n# EU residency failover response for Customer Support\n\nOwner: Platform Engineering  \nAudience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  \nScope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment\n\n## Reviewed support rule\n\nDo not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.\n- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.\n- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.\n- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. # EU residency failover response for Customer Support

Owner: Platform Engineering  
Audience: Customer Support, Incident Command, Routing, Security  
Scope: Redwood Hosted API tenants whose customer data may be subject to an EU residency commitment

## Reviewed support rule

Do not say that “EU customers always stay in the EU” based only on account location or tier. First verify the executed customer agreement and the live enforceable routing policy. For a tenant configured as EU-only, region-pinned, or with a custom EU boundary, Redwood may route only to a healthy region explicitly inside that boundary. If no allowed target is usable, the safe default is to deny the out-of-boundary action and degrade or stay put; it is not silent cross-border failover. Any boundary expansion during an incident requires Security approval, customer approval for Enterprise/regulated tenants, and an auditable, time-scoped change.

## Supported routing modes

- **Global:** data-plane processing may use any supported region. Self-serve/Standard Hosted and Enterprise Hosted are Global unless an explicit residency constraint has been configured; an EU address or Enterprise tier alone is not an EU-only control.
- **EU-only:** processing is limited to the tenant's configured EU region set, such as an explicitly allowed EU primary and EU secondary. Within-boundary failover is supported when the target is healthy and capable.
- **Region-pinned:** one allowed region. There is no cross-region failover; use load shedding, circuit breakers, Retry-After, or a service error while communicating the impairment.
- **Custom boundary:** a contract-defined allow-list. Failover is allowed only among listed regions.
- **Dedicated/Private distinction:** Dedicated follows its contracted deployment footprint and approved pools. Private residency is customer-controlled; this Hosted support response must not be used as a Private deployment guarantee.

describe disaster recovery as an automatic waiver.

For an enforced pinned workload, requests that would violate policy are blocked deterministically rather than silently sent elsewhere. When there is no in-boundary capacity, the operational result is degradation/stay-put, commonly a 503 or 429 with Retry-After and protective limits.

Sources: [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) (`dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`); [Hosted enforcement FAQ](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-residency-enforcement-faq.json) (`dsid_261a4ade6f21403185d98805521b1e1d`); [Hosted API Regional Failover runbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json) (`dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc`).

## KMS behavior

The enforced KMS path scopes key references by tenant and region. Admission/residency checks occur before key material is fetched; cross-region key usage is rejected when the key region does not match the request region. RBAC region claims are intersected with tenant regions. Audit entries carry region and key identifier context. Therefore, an allowed routing target is not usable until its region-qualified KMS binding is valid.

Support must determine whether the tenant uses Redwood-managed keys or a customer-managed KMS/HSM arrangement and must confirm migration/binding status. The merged implementation records a known limitation: cross-region read-only audit streams are not automatically migrated and require operator action. Do not assert that all legacy bindings or audit streams follow a routing change automatically.

Source: [Merged residency/KMS/RBAC implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-86107-introduce-data-residency-guards-kms-scoping-and-rbac-mapping.json) (`dsid_dc53eb164da14c6ca5fe90eadc134e11`).
